Why this analysis?

A change in yield shows that performance has moved, but not where the problem started. This project connects production outcomes, process measurements and equipment history to define a focused investigation.

Manufacturing Overview

Understand the route, then connect process measurements to quality outcomes.

Simplified process view
01Wafer preparationClean and prepare the silicon surface.
02Film depositionAdd insulating, conductive or semiconductor layers.
03Pattern & etchTransfer patterns and remove selected material.
04Doping & planarizationModify properties and flatten the surface.
Operations repeat across layers; this is not a strictly linear sequence.
STAGE 01

Wafer Fabrication

Build transistors and interconnects on silicon.

Silicon wafers undergo repeated cycles of thin-film deposition, photolithography, etching, ion implantation and chemical mechanical planarization (CMP). These processes create and connect the transistor structures that form integrated circuits.

Engineers monitor

Critical Dimension (CD) and overlay; film thickness and uniformity; defect density and wafer yield.

Output

A processed wafer containing integrated circuits, ready for wafer-level electrical testing.

STAGE 02

Assembly & Packaging

Separate functional dies, establish electrical connections and protect the silicon chip.

The processed wafer is diced into individual dies. Selected dies are attached to a package substrate, electrically interconnected through wire bonding or flip-chip technology, and protected using underfill, encapsulation or a thermal management structure, depending on package design.

Engineers monitor

Die placement accuracy and alignment; bond quality and interconnection integrity; underfill/encapsulation quality and package warpage.

Output

An assembled semiconductor package with external electrical connections.

Simplified process view
01Wafer dicingSeparate selected dies from the wafer.
02Die attachMount the die on the package structure.
03InterconnectionWire bonds or flip-chip bumps connect the die.
04Protection & finishingAdd materials and thermal structures as required.
Wire bonding and flip-chip are alternative interconnect routes.
Simplified process view
01Electrical testingCheck electrical and functional behavior.
02Performance screeningEvaluate speed, power and operating limits.
03Burn-in & reliabilityApply defined stress where required.
04Final inspectionConfirm applicable release requirements.
Wafer probing precedes dicing. Stress and reliability checks follow the product/test plan.
STAGE 03

Testing & Inspection

Verify functionality and electrical performance, with reliability assessments according to the product/test plan.

Packaged devices undergo automated electrical and functional testing. Engineers evaluate performance against product specifications, screen manufacturing failures and conduct reliability assessments under defined conditions where required.

Engineers monitor

Functional pass/fail rate; power, frequency and electrical performance; failure rate, reliability evidence and final-test yield.

Output

Screened products meeting applicable release requirements.

Possible defects by manufacturing stage

Wafer Fabrication

DIE FUNCTIONALITY & YIELD
  • Particle contamination: pattern defects.
  • Pattern bridging: unintended electrical shorts.
  • Etch nonuniformity: dimensional variation.
  • Film defects: voids, cracks or poor adhesion.
Detection: Optical inspection, CD-SEM, film metrology and wafer testing.

Assembly & Packaging

PACKAGE INTEGRITY & CONNECTIVITY
  • Die cracking: stress damages the silicon.
  • Bonding defects: incomplete electrical paths.
  • Delamination: separation between materials.
  • Voids: risks to joint or thermal integrity.
Detection: Optical inspection, X-ray, acoustic microscopy and electrical testing.

Testing & Inspection

PRODUCT QUALITY & RELIABILITY
  • Functional failure: operating requirements not met.
  • Electrical failure: current, voltage or timing outside limits.
  • Intermittent failure: inconsistent behavior.
  • Stress-related failure: degradation under defined tests.
Detection: ATE, functional testing and reliability testing.

Educational examples extend beyond the seven simulated event categories. Failures detected during testing are not proof that testing caused the defect.

Ball Grid Array (BGA)

Encapsulation / protection
Silicon die
Flip-chip bumps + underfill
Package substrate: routing & support
●●●●●●●●
Solder balls: package-to-PCB joints
PCB
Illustrative flip-chip BGA cross-section; not to scale.

Two Electrical Interfaces

BGA connects a semiconductor package to a PCB through an array of solder balls. The package substrate routes electrical signals between the silicon die and the external board.

  • Die-to-substrate: Flip-chip bumps connect the silicon die to the substrate.
  • Package-to-board: Solder balls connect the substrate to the PCB.

The substrate provides electrical routing and mechanical support, while the package protects the silicon die.

Surface Mount Technology (SMT)

SMT mounts packaged components onto a PCB. Paste printing, placement and reflow form the solder joints; inspection checks the resulting assembly.

Paste printing→SPI→Placement→Reflow→AOI→X-ray where appropriate

Semiconductor packaging connects and protects the die. PCB-level SMT mounts the package onto the board and is not simulated in this dataset.

Technical schema and data dictionary
Manufacturing relational model

Colored headers distinguish genealogy, execution, evidence and reference tables. Connectors show principal relationships; extra validated foreign keys are listed in the entity fields.

lotsPK lot_id · 120 rows

Parent of wafers (1:N); product and period context.

wafersPK wafer_id · 3,000 rows

FK lot_id. Parent of tracked packages and wafer runs.

packagesPK package_id · 24,000 rows

FK wafer_id, lot_id. Unique source wafer + die_site.

process_runsPK run_id · 119,566 rows

FK wafer_id, lot_id, process_id, subdivision_id; package_id only for package runs.

measurementsPK measurement_id · 59,898 rows

FK run_id. Sampled 0..1 observation per run.

defectsPK defect_id · 1,200 rows

FK run_id, defect_code. Multiple events can refer to a unit.

test_resultsPK test_id · 24,221 rows

FK package_id, run_id, subdivision_id. One package/attempt; retests use original final-test run.

equipment_eventsPK event_id · 3 rows

FK subdivision_id. Timestamped intervention.

process_stepsPK process_id · 12 rows

Process reference: stage, unit level, parameter and illustrative specifications.

equipmentPK subdivision_id · 32 rows

PK subdivision_id; FK process_id. equipment_id groups subdivisions.

defect_catalogPK defect_code · 7 rows

FK process_id. Educational event definitions.

Yield & Defect Analysis

Locate the loss, then inspect the process behind it.

Observed performance

Package assembly yield changed -3.08 percentage points from reference to disturbance.

Final electrical test: 3.97% failed screens (935/23,566 runs).

Scope: 3,000 touched wafers; 24,000 tracked packages; 1,200 events / 119,566 observed runs. No cross-stage yield multiplication is implied.

Reference, disturbance and post-action are predefined simulation periods. The colored windows do not establish causality or verified corrective-action effectiveness.

Observed loss and investigation priority

Reference: 39 failed / 7,964 packages (0.49% failure rate).

Disturbance: 359 failed / 10,061 packages (3.57% failure rate).

Post-action: 36 failed / 5,975 packages (0.60% failure rate).

Impact: Package assembly yield changed -3.08 percentage points from reference to disturbance. This is not an estimate of units saved or financial loss.

Next check: Final electrical test: 3.97% failed screens (935/23,566 runs). Compare the same process across equipment and periods before assigning a cause.

Metric definitions and filter scope

Reference: source lots 1–40; disturbance: 41–90; post-action: 91–120. These are fixed simulation windows.

Fab yield = passing wafers / touched completed wafers. Assembly yield = packages passing all assembly screens / touched tracked packages. Final first-pass = passing attempt-1 packages / selected final-test packages. Retest recovery = passing attempt-2 packages / retested packages, not all first-pass failures.

Inclusive date filters use run-end time. Touched units define the cohort; whole-route unit flags are then used. Final metrics include attempts linked to selected final-test runs even if a retest timestamp is later. Assembly failures are held out of final testing. Events are not defective-unit counts; process failures can repeat on a unit.

Can this stream meet specifications?

Capability: detected instability
Full-study mean 1.958 um; overall SD 3.218; within sigma 1.406. Specifications are illustrative, not control limits.

Engineering implication

Evidence: Full study: 764 Individuals and 42 MR signals across 2,982 observations. Disturbance mean shift: +4.58 um versus reference.

Impact: detected instability makes a single capability index unsuitable for this study. Signals define a review scope, not a defective-unit count.

Next check: inspect the first-signal window and compare matched periods on the same subdivision. Independently verify metrology before assigning a physical cause.

Method & assumptions
period n mean sd
Reference 963 0.007 1.511
Disturbance 1267 4.587 3.046
Post-action 752 0.025 1.501

I-MR uses chronological observations, not daily averages. First 40 points estimate frozen limits; minimum 20. Within sigma = baseline mean MR / 1.128. I limits = baseline mean ± 3 × within sigma. MR UCL = 3.267 × baseline mean MR; MR LCL = 0.

Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6 × within sigma). Cpk = min(USL − mean, mean − LSL)/(3 × within sigma). Cp describes spread; Cpk also reflects centering. Overall sample SD is reported separately.

Capability requires 30 observations and is withheld for detected I/MR instability, zero variation or failed normality screening (alpha .01). Only beyond-3-sigma rules are implemented. No-signal and normality tests do not establish independence, stability or MSA adequacy.

Display navigation never changes the study, baseline or Cp/Cpk. The first displayed MR can use the immediate preceding observation outside the display. No gaps are bridged. A new Statistical study may refit its own illustrative baseline.

Independent Cp/Cpk teaching example

Separate fixed normal quantiles in deterministic shuffled order; not manufacturing observations and not evidence about the selected equipment. The same screening functions return Cp 1.504 and Cpk 1.203, n=100, LSL=96, USL=106 arbitrary units. No screening bypass or manufacturing resampling.

Root Cause Investigation

Use evidence to prioritize hypotheses, not to manufacture certainty.

Problem and observed evidence

E09A-H2 shows the largest observed mean shift: +4.58 um (reference n=963; disturbance n=1,267).

Highest selected-process event rate: E09A-H2: 4.35 events per 100 runs (259/5,948).

These associations prioritize a review. They do not confirm a physical root cause.
Lots in scope
120
Parameter observations
12,000
Selected-process events
355
Assembly-failing packages
434
24,000 touched tracked packages

Impact and next verification

Evidence: E09A-H2 shows the largest observed mean shift: +4.58 um (reference n=963; disturbance n=1,267).

Observed cohort impact: 434 assembly-failing packages / 24,000 tracked packages in scope. Disturbance yield differs from reference by -3.08 percentage points.

Boundary: these are whole-route assembly outcomes, not failures proven to originate at the selected step.

Next check: independently verify the measurement system, inspect equipment history and run a matched-product/lot comparison before confirming the mechanism.
